items.title: 68239_Ram Ramirez oral history interview
items.q: But Earl Hines came over and made this record, and his style was so unorthodox

ctx.x: "Soliloquy." And these... It was a very... It was quite a business. Publishers used to put out these various booklets and sheet music. For instance, if there was a popular song, you know, like a (?), they would put it out not only in sheet music form for the vocal, but also different, various pianists, the way they would play it. Well, Rube Bloom(?) was one of them with piano solos... They were very interesting. And of course, at that time, I just couldn't find one that has this "57 Varieties". Man, that's rough!
But Earl Hines came over and made this record, and his style was so unorthodox; you know, you had to really have the hands in order to play it.
Earl's hands were not that bag.
